Saturday, November 14

Game recap

NYR5VAN1Final: NYR 5, VAN 1

Vancouver hung around for a period, which at this point counts as a moral victory. Elias Pettersson opened the scoring at 12:13 of the first, Gabe Perreault answered before intermission, and then the second period happened: four Rangers goals in 7:49. Oliver Bjorkstrand scored on the power play, Glenn Gawdin got his first NHL goal unassisted, Alexis Lafrenière buried his 10th, and Gawdin added his second just 56 seconds later. A guy who played 7:59 had two goals; the entire Canucks lineup had one. J.T. Miller set up two against his old team, Dylan Garand stopped 27 of 28, and Leevi Meriläinen made 26 saves on 31. New York is 12-8-1. Vancouver is 3-17-1 with seven straight losses, and the only thing the Canucks are building right now is a lottery ticket.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NSH3VGK2SOFinal: NSH 3, VGK 2 SO

Vegas threw 42 shots at Juuse Saros and got two past him, so naturally this one needed a shootout. Ryan O'Reilly scored at 7:56 of the first, Victor Olofsson tied it, and Rasmus Andersson put Vegas ahead in the second. O'Reilly tied it again at 9:44 of the third, his second of the night and ninth of the season, and overtime settled nothing. In the shootout Trevor Connelly scored for Vegas, Filip Forsberg answered, Jack Eichel was stopped and Roman Josi ended it, after playing 31:40 and apparently still having legs. Saros made 40 saves; Adin Hill made 30 on 32. Nashville has won seven straight and is 11-4-5. Vegas outshot its guests by 10 and went home with one point, which in that town is called breaking even and still feels like losing.

Friday, November 13

Game recap

CAR4SEA1Final: CAR 4, SEA 1

The NHL flew Seattle across an ocean to play a home game in Helsinki, and the Kraken honored the occasion with 13 shots, roughly what Carolina's fourth line puts up on a slow Tuesday. Nikolaj Ehlers opened the scoring at 11:44 of the first, Sebastian Aho added a power-play goal 66 seconds later, and Juuso Välimäki made it 3-0 in the second. Aho finished the job with his 12th of the year in the third, while K'Andre Miller and Logan Stankoven had two assists each. Brandon Bussi stopped 12 of 13, which barely counts as working, and Frederick Gaudreau spoiled the shutout with 6:45 left. Philipp Grubauer made 26 saves on 30 shots. The Canes are 15-3-2, tied with Minnesota for the league lead at 32 points. The two teams do it again Saturday in Finland, so Seattle gets one more shot at finding the Carolina net, or failing that, some decent sightseeing.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

MTL5BOS2Final: MTL 5, BOS 2

Boston's four-game win streak lasted exactly as long as it took Montreal to walk into TD Garden. The Habs scored the first five goals: Kirby Dach at 2:34, Josh Anderson in the first, then Jake Evans, an unassisted Cole Caufield (his 12th) and Phillip Danault in the second. Jeremy Swayman was pulled after four goals on 17 shots, and Michael DiPietro stopped 13 of 14 in relief, which is the kind of relief that comes after the house has already burned down. Casey Mittelstadt scored twice for Boston, late in the second and 53 seconds into the third, with Elias Lindholm assisting both, but Jacob Fowler shut the door with 30 saves on 32 shots. Montreal is 12-3-4, tied with Tampa Bay for the Atlantic lead at 28 points, and 8-0-2 in its last 10. That's the kind of run Bruins fans used to think was their birthright, and now they get to watch it in the other sweater.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

MIN5TOR2Final: MIN 5, TOR 2

Matt Boldy brought his own hat to Scotiabank Arena and left with everyone else's. Boldy opened the scoring late in the first, tied it on the power play in the second and put Minnesota ahead for good 3:59 into the third, a hat trick with Kirill Kaprizov assisting the first two. In between, Toronto actually led: Auston Matthews scored his 12th and Zack MacEwen made it 2-1 early in the second, a lead that lasted a little under three minutes. Michael McCarron added a fourth and Danila Yurov hit the empty net, giving Kaprizov his third assist. Jesper Wallstedt made 26 saves on 28 shots; Anthony Stolarz stopped 21 of 25. The Wild are 14-3-4 and tied for the league lead at 32 points. The Leafs are 8-11-2, have lost five straight and are 3-7-0 in their last 10, and somewhere in Toronto a man is already pricing out April tee times.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

COL3OTT4OTFinal: COL 3, OTT 4 OT

Shane Pinto started it and Shane Pinto finished it. He scored unassisted 7:11 in, Tim Stützle made it 2-0 later in the first, and Pinto won it alone again 2:08 into overtime. The middle was all Colorado, which played much of the night without Nathan MacKinnon and Cale Makar after both left in the second period with lower-body injuries. Artturi Lehkonen scored his 14th on the power play, Parker Kelly scored shorthanded early in the third, and Gabriel Landeskog put the Avalanche ahead 3-2 on another power play at 10:03. Drake Batherson tied it with 3:56 left. Linus Ullmark made 26 saves on 29 shots; Scott Wedgewood stopped 22 of 26. The Senators are 12-6-2 and fourth in the Atlantic. Colorado takes a point to Montreal for Saturday, plus a lesson: a one-goal lead with ten minutes left is a suggestion, not a plan.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

WSH2NJD5Final: WSH 2, NJD 5

Washington led in the second period, which in hindsight was just the Devils letting them hold it for a minute. Evan Rodrigues scored on the power play 2:20 in, Ryan Leonard answered on one of his own, and Pierre-Luc Dubois put the Capitals up 2-1 early in the second. That lasted 7:40. Lenni Hameenaho tied it with his first of the season, Vladislav Kolyachonok scored his first for the go-ahead goal 6:27 into the third, Stefan Noesen added one late, and Jack Hughes hit the empty net for his 10th. Rodrigues finished with a goal and an assist. Connor Hellebuyck made 26 saves on 28 shots; Logan Thompson stopped 24 of 28. New Jersey is 14-6-0 and 8-2-0 in its last 10, second in the Metropolitan. The Capitals are 10-7-0 with 67 games left, tied for the most in the league, which is a lot of hockey for a team that couldn't keep a lead for eight minutes.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

TBL3CBJ1Final: TBL 3, CBJ 1

Tampa Bay showed up in Columbus without Anthony Cirelli and Erik Cernak and still looked like the team with the plan. Brandon Hagel scored 2:57 in, Matthew Knies tied it on a Columbus power play, and then the two teams fought twice in two seconds: Mathieu Olivier with Scott Sabourin and Ryan Lomberg with Jeffrey Viel, 12:22 and 12:24 of the first. After that the Lightning went back to hockey. Jake Guentzel scored his 11th 1:06 into the third and Hagel added his 13th, with Nikita Kucherov assisting both of Hagel's goals. Dennis Hildeby stopped 28 of 29; Jet Greaves made 25 saves on 28 shots. Sean Monahan left late in the second with an upper-body injury. The Lightning are 13-4-2 and first in the Atlantic. Columbus is 7-10-0, last in the Metropolitan and on a three-game skid, and its best shift of the night was a two-second stretch with the gloves off.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

DET4FLA5Final: DET 4, FLA 5

Detroit led Florida 4-1 in the second period, and if you've watched the Red Wings lately you already know how this ends. J.T. Compher, Andreas Englund, Lucas Raymond and Marco Kasper (his first of the year) built the lead after Sam Reinhart's opener. Then Gustav Forsling scored with 18 seconds left in the second, Anton Lundell scored early in the third, Lars Eller tied it at 16:29, and Lundell won it 51 seconds later, with both Tkachuks assisting. Carter Verhaeghe had three assists. Akira Schmid made 24 saves on 28 shots; John Gibson stopped 24 of 29. Alex DeBrincat and Sam Bennett dropped the gloves in the second. The Panthers are 11-7-2 and have won two straight. The Red Wings are 7-10-3 and have lost five in a row, and blowing a three-goal lead in under 18 minutes is a fresh way to do it.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

BUF2CHI3OTFinal: BUF 2, CHI 3 OT

Buffalo went to Chicago, the softest landing spot in the Central, and still flew home with a loss. Owen Power opened the scoring, Frank Nazar answered on the power play with Connor Bedard assisting, and Tage Thompson's 12th, also on the power play, put the Sabres back up 2-1 after one. Then nobody scored for more than a period until Nazar tied it 8:22 into the third, and Ryan Donato won it 3:12 into overtime, set up by Anton Frondell and Sam Rinzel, who had two assists. Spencer Knight stopped 21 of 23; Alex Lyon made 22 saves on 25 shots. Chicago is still last in the Central at 5-13-1, but it has a win streak now, all one game of it. The Sabres are 8-7-4 and -13, and losing in overtime to the Blackhawks is one point in the standings and a new low everywhere else.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

WPG8DAL3Final: WPG 8, DAL 3

Dallas led 2-0 after one and 3-2 halfway through the game, and then Winnipeg scored the last six goals like it was running a drill. Arttu Hyry and Roope Hintz gave the Stars the early lead, Dylan Samberg and Mark Scheifele scored unassisted to tie it, and David Perron's first of the season put Dallas back ahead. After that: Dawson Mercer, a Scheifele power-play goal and Mercer again with nine seconds left in the second, then Kyle Connor (his 16th) a minute into the third, which ended Jake Oettinger's night at six goals on 27 shots. Gabriel Vilardi and Cole Koepke scored 14 seconds apart late, and Casey DeSmith stopped one of three. Scheifele, Connor and Vilardi each had three points; Stuart Skinner made 30 saves on 33 shots. The Jets have won five straight. The Stars held a players-only meeting afterward, which is what you do when eight goals on home ice needs a closed door.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

STL1UTA0SOFinal: STL 1, UTA 0 SO

Sixty-five minutes, zero goals, and the most exciting thing in regulation was Liam O'Brien and Ross Johnston fighting 1:56 in. Joel Hofer stopped all 29 Utah shots and Karel Vejmelka stopped all 22 from St. Louis, so the night went to a shootout that needed eight rounds. Vincent Trocheck and Jake Neighbours scored in the first, the next ten shooters all missed, then Michael Carcone and Jimmy Snuggerud traded goals in the seventh. Barrett Hayton was stopped in the eighth, and Connor McMichael ended it. The Blues are 9-8-2 and have won two straight. The Mammoth are 10-8-2 and 3-5-2 in their last 10, and they went two for eight in the shootout on the way to being shut out at home. Utah's offense is going the way of its mascot.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

Game recap

NYI5LAK2Final: NYI 5, LAK 2

The Islanders ended a four-game winless streak in Los Angeles, and Matthew Schaefer marked his 100th NHL game with a power-play goal, his sixth, to put them ahead 2-1 in the first. Brayden Schenn opened the scoring and finished with a goal and two assists, Victor Eklund made it 3-1 in the second, and Simon Holmstrom scored unassisted 39 seconds into the third before setting up Bo Horvat's empty-netter. Trevor Moore and Quinton Byfield, on a power play set up by Artemi Panarin and Kevin Fiala, scored for the Kings. Tony DeAngelo and Corey Perry fought in the second. Ilya Sorokin made 26 saves on 28 shots; Darcy Kuemper stopped 16 of 20. The Islanders are 8-6-4. The Kings are 5-10-2, have lost three straight and sit seventh in the Pacific, and the only thing keeping them out of the basement is Vancouver.

By Puckline Prince · Box score →

NYR 5–1 VAN

New York RangersNYR12-8-1 · 25 pts31 shots
5
FinalRogers Arena
1
Vancouver CanucksVAN3-17-1 · 7 pts28 shots
1st2nd3rdTNYR1405VAN1001

Puckline's Report

Vancouver hung around for a period, which at this point counts as a moral victory. Elias Pettersson opened the scoring at 12:13 of the first, Gabe Perreault answered before intermission, and then the second period happened: four Rangers goals in 7:49. Oliver Bjorkstrand scored on the power play, Glenn Gawdin got his first NHL goal unassisted, Alexis Lafrenière buried his 10th, and Gawdin added his second just 56 seconds later. A guy who played 7:59 had two goals; the entire Canucks lineup had one. J.T. Miller set up two against his old team, Dylan Garand stopped 27 of 28, and Leevi Meriläinen made 26 saves on 31. New York is 12-8-1. Vancouver is 3-17-1 with seven straight losses, and the only thing the Canucks are building right now is a lottery ticket.

By Puckline Prince

Vegas Golden KnightsVGK13-5-3 · 29 pts42 shots
1st2nd3rdOTSOTNSH101013VGK110002

Puckline's Report

Vegas threw 42 shots at Juuse Saros and got two past him, so naturally this one needed a shootout. Ryan O'Reilly scored at 7:56 of the first, Victor Olofsson tied it, and Rasmus Andersson put Vegas ahead in the second. O'Reilly tied it again at 9:44 of the third, his second of the night and ninth of the season, and overtime settled nothing. In the shootout Trevor Connelly scored for Vegas, Filip Forsberg answered, Jack Eichel was stopped and Roman Josi ended it, after playing 31:40 and apparently still having legs. Saros made 40 saves; Adin Hill made 30 on 32. Nashville has won seven straight and is 11-4-5. Vegas outshot its guests by 10 and went home with one point, which in that town is called breaking even and still feels like losing.

SEA @ CAR · 1:00 PM ET

Seattle KrakenSEA9-7-1 · 19 PTSML +320
@1:00 PM ETSat Nov 14 · Veikkaus Arena
SEA +320MLCAR -420
Carolina HurricanesCAR15-3-2 · 32 PTSML -420

Puckline Preview

Round two in Helsinki, and Seattle would like a word. Carolina took Thursday's opener 4-1, with Sebastian Aho scoring twice, the first on the power play, in his first NHL game on Finnish ice, and Frederick Gaudreau getting the Kraken's only goal. The Hurricanes (15-3-2, first in the league at 4.10 goals a game) can now sweep the Global Series. Pyotr Kochetkov (11-1-0) projects in net after Brandon Bussi took Thursday. Jordan Staal is a morning decision after missing 14 games with a torn calf, and Alexander Nikishin projects back in on defense. Seattle projects Joey Daccord in goal and may give prospect Jagger Firkus his NHL debut, with Ryan Lindgren and Jacob Melanson game-time decisions.

The Kraken's real problem is the penalty kill: 65.2%, 30th in the league, against a team that already scored on the power play in this building two nights ago. Seattle flew halfway around the world to be the supporting cast in a Finnish homecoming, and so far it has played the part well. Win, and the Kraken fly home with a split and a story. Lose, and it's a very long flight with the penalty-kill tape for company.

By Puckline Prince

Puckline Preview

Winnipeg rolls into the United Center on a five-game win streak, fresh off an 8-3 beatdown in Dallas in which Mark Scheifele tied Dale Hawerchuk's franchise points record. One more point and it's his alone, and Chicago's defense has been generous about that sort of thing. Kyle Connor already has 16 goals. Dallas cost the Jets, though: Dylan DeMelo is on IR, week to week, Isak Rosen is out, and defenseman Henry Thrun is up from Manitoba. NHL.com lists Nico Daws first in goal, ahead of Stuart Skinner.

Chicago (5-13-1) finally exhaled Thursday, beating Buffalo 3-2 in overtime on two Frank Nazar goals, five days after Carolina hung nine on them. Connor Bedard leads the team with 15 points, Patrick Kane is back on the second line, Spencer Knight projects in net, and Bowen Byram misses a 13th straight game. Here's the twist: the October meeting went Chicago's way, 4-3 in overtime, so the Hawks have already beaten this team once, which is more than their record would lead you to believe. A 2:30 local start means Chicago fans can be disappointed before dinner, or, for once, not.

By Puckline Prince

MIN @ BOS · 7:00 PM ET

Minnesota WildMIN14-3-4 · 32 PTSML -120
@7:00 PM ETSat Nov 14 · TD Garden
MIN -120MLBOS +100
Boston BruinsBOS13-5-1 · 27 PTSML +100

Puckline Preview

The Wild arrive as the West's leaders and the league's hottest road team: 8-0-2 in their last 10, seven straight road wins, and a 5-2 win in Toronto on Thursday in which Matt Boldy scored a hat trick. Kirill Kaprizov has 35 points (17 goals), Quinn Hughes has 28, and Jesper Wallstedt (.925, 1.94) projects in goal again. Two questions hang over them: Joel Eriksson Ek left Thursday after a collision with Jake McCabe (John Hynes thinks he's OK), and Brock Faber could make his season debut, though Hynes says it isn't a guarantee.

Boston (13-5-1) had been cruising at home until Montreal walked into TD Garden on Thursday and won 5-2. It was the Bruins' first home loss since Oct. 5, and Jeremy Swayman got the hook after four goals on 17 shots. Marco Sturm spent Friday on video and shuffling his defense pairs, which is coach for "we were bad." Swayman projects back in. Minnesota already beat Boston 4-1 on Oct. 3, handing the Bruins their first loss of the season. Boston would like the rematch to go differently and would settle for its goalie seeing the third period.

EDM @ TOR · 7:00 PM ET

Edmonton OilersEDM14-3-3 · 31 PTSML -152
@7:00 PM ETSat Nov 14 · Scotiabank Arena
EDM -152MLTOR +126
Toronto Maple LeafsTOR8-11-2 · 18 PTSML +126

Puckline Preview

Connor McDavid brings a 20-game point streak to Toronto: a point in every game Edmonton has played, 49 in all. He's the fourth player ever to open a season that way, and he did it last season too. Leon Draisaitl (37 points) and Evan Bouchard (33) aren't exactly passengers, and the Oilers (14-3-3) have won three straight, the last on Bouchard's overtime winner against Philadelphia. Edmonton also gets another look at the Leafs team that beat it 7-2 in Edmonton on Oct. 24.

That Toronto feels like a long time ago. The Leafs are 8-11-2 and have lost five straight, all at home, and seven of their last eight. Jim Hiller says the team still sees progress, which is the official language of a five-game losing streak. Morgan Rielly has no update, Kirill Marchenko is still working his way back, and Colton Sissons is on IR. As of Friday, Hiller hadn't chosen between Sergei Bobrovsky, who has lost his last five starts, and Anthony Stolarz. Chris Tanev does return. Saturday night at Scotiabank Arena, with McDavid in town and the boos already warmed up: Leafs fans have suffered worse, but rarely with this many witnesses.

By Puckline Prince

COL @ MTL · 7:00 PM ET

Colorado AvalancheCOL11-6-3 · 25 PTSML +104
@7:00 PM ETSat Nov 14 · Centre Bell
COL +104MLMTL -125
Montreal CanadiensMTL12-3-4 · 28 PTSML -125

Puckline Preview

Saturday night at the Bell Centre, and the Avalanche may show up without the two players who make them the Avalanche. Nathan MacKinnon (30 points) and Cale Makar (23) both left Thursday's 4-3 overtime loss in Ottawa with lower-body injuries, and Adrian Dater reports neither plays tonight. Colorado hadn't confirmed it Friday night and expects to say more this morning. The Avs called up Gavin Brindley, who leads their AHL club with 16 points in 13 games, and brought rookie defenseman Alex Gagne along in case he's needed. This is a team that gave up seven in Columbus on Nov. 3, so the margin for error is about the width of a skate blade.

Montreal, meanwhile, is having the kind of November that gets the city drawing up parade routes nobody asked for: 12-3-4 and a 12-game point streak (9-0-3), capped by a 5-2 win in Boston. Jacob Fowler made 30 saves there and is 9-1-2 with a .926, and Cole Caufield has 12 goals. The one cloud: Chris Kreider left Thursday's game in the third period and there's been no update. First meeting of the season, so no grudges yet. Give it 60 minutes.

By Puckline Prince

DET @ TBL · 7:00 PM ET

Detroit Red WingsDET7-10-3 · 17 PTSML +176
@7:00 PM ETSat Nov 14 · Benchmark International Arena
DET +176MLTBL -215
Tampa Bay LightningTBL13-4-2 · 28 PTSML -215

Puckline Preview

The Red Wings roll into Tampa with five straight losses, the latest a 5-4 loss in Florida on Thursday after leading 4-1, which takes real talent. They're 7-10-3, seven points out of a playoff spot, and Dylan Larkin isn't walking through that door: he has been suspended without pay since Oct. 29 in his trade standoff. Pierre LeBrun hears "a lot of hurt feelings" on both sides, and Chris Johnston says Detroit doesn't see a workable deal with any of the 10 teams on Larkin's list. A decade without playoff hockey, and now the soap opera has a cliffhanger.

Tampa is 13-4-2, a perfect 8-0-0 at home and 6-1-2 in its last nine, and Nikita Kucherov is cooking: a natural hat trick in Buffalo on Wednesday and a team-high 28 points in a contract year, with David Pagnotta already penciling in Toronto and Montreal as July suitors. Brandon Hagel has five goals in three games. The Bolts are banged up, though: Brayden Point is reportedly on IR, and Anthony Cirelli and Erik Cernak are day to day after missing Thursday. Tampa won the first meeting 4-2 on Nov. 3. Both penalty kills sit in the bottom eight, so somebody's power play could eat well.

OTT @ PIT · 7:00 PM ET

Ottawa SenatorsOTT12-6-2 · 26 PTSML -128
@7:00 PM ETSat Nov 14 · PPG Paints Arena
OTT -128MLPIT +106
Pittsburgh PenguinsPIT7-10-2 · 16 PTSML +106

Puckline Preview

Ottawa comes to Pittsburgh at 12-6-2 and 3-0-1 in its last four, fresh off Shane Pinto's birthday party on Thursday: two goals, three points and the overtime winner against Colorado. Linus Ullmark made 26 saves in his first game back after missing nine, though Ottawa hasn't said who starts tonight, Ullmark or Samuel Ersson. Nick Cousins is still out after Jakob Chychrun's hit Tuesday, and Bruce Garrioch says GM Steve Staios is shopping for forward help in a market that's jammed up.

The Penguins are 7-10-2, which is not what you want with a combined 79 years of Crosby and Malkin on the top line. Malkin, at 40, just became the first player that age to assist on six straight team goals, so the old man is fine; it's the rest of it. Sergei Murashov looks set to start after winning his last two, including 36 saves in a shootout win in San Jose, per Pittsburgh Hockey Now (not confirmed). That's a promotion over Arturs Silovs and his .873. And Erik Karlsson's name keeps coming up: Pierre LeBrun says his camp meets Kyle Dubas in the new year, with Carolina waiting if talks open. First meeting of the season.

NJD @ WSH · 7:00 PM ET

New Jersey DevilsNJD14-6-0 · 28 PTSML -120
@7:00 PM ETSat Nov 14 · Capital One Arena
NJD -120MLWSH +100
Washington CapitalsWSH10-7-0 · 20 PTSML +100

Puckline Preview

Part two of the home-and-home, and the Capitals have had two days to think about Thursday's 5-2 loss in Newark, where the Devils got three straight goals from three guys who were in Utica earlier in the week: Lenni Hameenaho, Stefan Noesen and Vladislav Kolyachonok, whose goal in his first game as a Devil stood as the winner. The season series is 1-1 after Washington won 4-2 on Oct. 17. New Jersey is 14-6-0 and 10-2-0 in its last 12, and Connor Hellebuyck, confirmed by the team for both games, is 6-0-0 with a .916. The blue line is getting patched together, though: Johnathan Kovacevic is on IR, Brett Pesce is day to day with an illness, and 2024 10th pick Anton Silaev got his first call-up for this one.

On the other bench, Alex Ovechkin has gone 11 straight games without a goal and has one in 16, at a career-low 13:47 a night in his final season. Spencer Carbery likes the underlying numbers, which is coach for "the puck owes him." Pierre-Luc Dubois has scored in three straight, and Logan Thompson has started the last five, though no starter has been named yet.

PHI @ CBJ · 7:00 PM ET

Philadelphia FlyersPHI5-10-6 · 16 PTSML +112
@7:00 PM ETSat Nov 14 · Nationwide Arena
PHI +112MLCBJ -134
Columbus Blue JacketsCBJ7-10-0 · 14 PTSML -134

Puckline Preview

Two of the league's three lowest-scoring offenses meet in Columbus, so keep the remote handy. Philadelphia (5-10-6) is 31st at 2.24 goals a game and is 0-6 in games that go past regulation, which takes a special kind of talent. Columbus (7-10-0) is 30th at 2.47, has lost three straight, and has a power play (26th) and penalty kill (24th) that are both shopping in the bargain bin. The one meeting so far went the Jackets' way: Kent Johnson scored twice in a 4-3 overtime win in Philadelphia on Oct. 27.

The Flyers' loudest noise is off the ice. Matvei Michkov leads them with 10 goals while his name keeps surfacing in trade chatter: the team and Michkov deny he asked out, but his former agent claimed on a Russian podcast that he will push for one. That's a rumor, not a fact. Columbus could be thin up front, with Conor Garland on IR and Sean Monahan day to day after leaving Thursday's loss to Tampa Bay. Philly hosts Edmonton on Sunday, so watch which goalie gets the road half of the back-to-back. Two teams starving for goals: somebody has to score eventually. Probably.

By Puckline Prince

FLA @ STL · 7:00 PM ET

Florida PanthersFLA11-7-2 · 24 PTSML -115
@7:00 PM ETSat Nov 14 · Enterprise Center
FLA -115MLSTL -104
St Louis BluesSTL9-8-2 · 20 PTSML -104

Puckline Preview

It's Big Walt night in St. Louis. The Blues celebrate Keith Tkachuk's Hall of Fame induction, and the two most famous Tkachuks of the current era will be in the visiting room: Matthew (a team-high 28 points) and Brady (10 goals in his first 20 games as a Panther) both play for Florida. Awkward for the ushers.

Florida (11-7-2) arrives after storming back from 4-1 down to beat Detroit 5-4 on Thursday, with Anton Lundell scoring twice, including the late winner. Tonight is the front half of a back-to-back, with Dallas waiting Sunday, and the Panthers are still without Aleksander Barkov and Brad Marchand. They also lead the league in penalty minutes, so the Blues' 20th-ranked power play should get plenty of reps. St. Louis (9-8-2) has won two straight, the latest a 1-0 eight-round shootout in Utah where Joel Hofer stopped everything. Jimmy Snuggerud leads the Blues with 10 goals, seven in his last 12 games. The Blues swept Florida last season, outscoring them 11-6, and are chasing their first three-game win streak of the year. As for the Panthers, they missed the playoffs last spring and have been trying ever since to remember how to be annoying in the good way.

By Puckline Prince

BUF @ DAL · 8:00 PM ET

Buffalo SabresBUF8-7-4 · 20 PTSML +114
@8:00 PM ETSat Nov 14 · American Airlines Center
BUF +114MLDAL -137
Dallas StarsDAL10-6-2 · 22 PTSML -137

Puckline Preview

Dallas spent Friday trying to scrub off an 8-3 beating from Winnipeg, the kind of night that ends with Jake Oettinger pulled after six goals and the locker room door shut for a players-only meeting. Jamie Benn said it needed to happen; Glen Gulutzan called it a mindset problem. The Stars (10-6-2) now have to fix it without Miro Heiskanen, who sits again but could be back Sunday, and Lian Bichsel, out a couple of weeks. Kyle Capobianco is out too, and Kyle Burroughs is reportedly coming up from Texas to plug the blue line. Oettinger is expected back in net, and he shut Buffalo out 4-0 on Oct. 8.

Buffalo (8-7-4) brings a three-game skid and special teams that need a search party: a 29th-ranked power play and a 28th-ranked penalty kill, facing a Dallas PK that ranks third. The Sabres are also 31st on faceoffs while Dallas leads the league, so expect Buffalo to spend a lot of the night chasing. Tage Thompson leads the Sabres with 21 points and has 14 in 15 career games against Dallas, but Mikko Rantanen has 27 points in 19 career games against Buffalo. The Stars have points in nine of the last 11 meetings.

By Puckline Prince

SJS @ UTA · 9:00 PM ET

San Jose SharksSJS8-11-2 · 18 PTSML +164
@9:00 PM ETSat Nov 14 · Delta Center
SJS +164MLUTA -200
Utah MammothUTA10-8-2 · 22 PTSML -200

Puckline Preview

The Mammoth come home 0-2-2 in their last four, capped by a 1-0 shootout loss to St. Louis in which Karel Vejmelka stopped all 22 shots and still lost. Logan Cooley, Utah's goal leader with 11, won't play tonight and isn't expected back this week while the team waits on test results, Andre Tourigny said. Dylan Guenther, Nate Schmidt and John Marino are on injured reserve, and Nick Schmaltz missed Thursday with a lower-body injury. The power play still hums at 34.3 percent (2nd), while the penalty kill (71.2 percent, 26th) keeps handing out free samples.

San Jose arrives 8-11-2 after spending part of Friday sitting on a grounded plane, which may be the only time this season the Sharks have been stopped from going backwards. Macklin Celebrini just passed 200 career points and leads the team with 23, but the Sharks score 2.52 goals a game (28th), and only one of their eight wins came by more than a goal. They are 4-0 in 3-on-3 overtime, so a tie game late is home turf. Alexander Wennberg is a game-time decision, and Sam Dickinson has been on the top power-play unit. First meeting of the season.

By Puckline Prince

Puckline Preview

The Islanders finally found a win Thursday, 5-2 in Los Angeles, to end a four-game winless run. Rookie Victor Eklund has scored in four straight, with Brayden Schenn setting up six of his seven goals, and Matthew Schaefer scored in his 100th NHL game. Jean-Gabriel Pageau is day to day with a lower-body injury after sitting out that win, and Mathew Barzal still hasn't played this season (one report says the Isles are eyeing Tuesday at home; the team hasn't said). The Isles' power play converts 16.1 percent, 28th in the league, which makes every penalty they draw feel like a courtesy.

Anaheim is the mirror image: the NHL's best power play at 36.8 percent, Cutter Gauthier with goals in seven straight games and a league-high 10 on the man advantage, and Leo Carlsson with 26 points. The catch is the other end. The Ducks allow 3.68 goals a game, their .863 team save percentage is second-worst in the league, and they just sent Laurent Brossoit back to San Diego after he won four of his five starts. That leaves Lukas Dostal or Ville Husso, with no starter named yet. The Ducks are 7-3-0 on the road and 3-5-1 at home. New York won the first meeting 3-2 on Oct. 20, when Anaheim managed 17 shots.

By Puckline Prince

CGY @ LAK · 10:00 PM ET

Calgary FlamesCGY8-10-1 · 17 PTSML +142
@10:00 PM ETSat Nov 14 · Crypto.com Arena
CGY +142MLLAK -172
Los Angeles KingsLAK5-10-2 · 12 PTSML -172

Puckline Preview

The Kings close a seven-game homestand tonight at 5-10-2, on a three-game skid and 2-7-0 at Crypto.com Arena, the kind of home record that has season-ticket holders asking whether parking is refundable. Thursday's 5-2 loss to the Islanders did come with a good moment: Kevin Fiala played his first game since breaking his leg at the Olympics nine months ago and picked up an assist in 16:37. Artemi Panarin leads the team with 19 points, though all six of his November points are assists, and Darcy Kuemper just played his 500th NHL game. The penalty kill sits at 66.1 percent, 29th in the league.

Calgary isn't cruising either at 8-10-1, scoring 2.47 goals a game (29th), but its power play is fourth at 29.5 percent, and the Flames are 6-1-0 against LA since the start of 2024-25. Adam Klapka moved up to Morgan Frost and Yegor Sharangovich's line after a season-high 16:07 and a power-play goal against the Rangers. Jonathan Huberdeau isn't on the trip, Kevin Bahl is out for the season, and this is the front end of a back-to-back with Anaheim on Sunday, so watch the Dustin Wolf and Devin Cooley split. Trade chatter lists Zach Whitecloud, Frost and Ryan Strome as names to watch; those are reports, not anything the team has said.

By Puckline Prince
